extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, national patent offices, European Patent Office staff, and judges/advisers involved in European patent practice
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for filing, examining, opposing, appealing, and enforcing European patent applications and European patents under the European Patent Convention (EPC). Covers substantive patentability criteria, formal filing and language requirements, procedural stages (search, examination, opposition, appeal), and effects of grant/revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable inventions (Article 52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentable inventions — patents shall be granted for any inventions which are susceptible of industrial application, are new and involve an inventive step, subject to the provisions of the Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the general requirement that an invention must be new, involve an inventive step and be industrially applicable; see also the specific Articles on novelty, inventive step and industrial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to patentability (Article 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to patentability — certain subject-matter and activities shall not be regarded as inventions for the purpose of patentability under the Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categories excluded from patentability (policy-driven exclusions are referenced in the Convention and implementing regulations); used to assess whether subject-matter is in principle eligible for a European patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Article 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty — an invention is considered new if it does not form part of the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the absolute novelty requirement against prior art; critical for assessing whether claimed subject-matter is new at filing or priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosures / Grace periods (Article 55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-prejudicial disclosures — certain disclosures are not to be taken into account for the purpose of assessing novelty or inventive step under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines cases where disclosures (e.g., due to evident abuse, display at official exhibitions) do not destroy novelty; check the Article and Implementing Regulations for conditions and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Article 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step — an invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for non-obviousness; used in substantive examination and opposition/appeal proceedings to evaluate whether claims are inventive over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Article 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial application — an invention is susceptible of industrial application if it can be made or used in any kind of industry, including agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures practical utility; lack of industrial application can be a ground to refuse or revoke a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements of the European patent application (Articles 75–83 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of the European patent application and requirements of the European patent application — formal content and documents to be submitted on filing (designation, disclosure, claims, abstract, drawings where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what must be included at filing (e.g., request, description, claims, drawings), how divisional applications are treated, designation of States, and other formalities that determine filing date and admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing (Article 76/related provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of filing — rules determining the date of filing of a European patent application (what documents are required to establish a filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for priority/novelty assessments; check which minimal items (e.g., indication that an application is being made and information identifying applicant and invention) secure a filing date under the Convention/Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Articles listed under Part III headings and Art.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention — the application must relate to one invention or to a group of inventions linked so as to form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in search and examination; lack of unity can lead to restriction or partial searches and affects divisional practice and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of the invention / Sufficiency (Article 83 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the invention — the European patent application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency of disclosure is a substantive requirement; inadequate disclosure can be a ground for refusal or revocation and limits the allowable scope of claims and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: The claims (Article 84 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims — claims must define the matter for which protection is sought and be clear and concise and supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims determine the extent of protection; Article 84 and implementing rules govern clarity, conciseness and support by the description; claim drafting must satisfy these for grant and to avoid objections during examination and opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: The abstract (Part III heading / Implementing Regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract — a brief summary of the technical disclosure of the invention must be provided as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract facilitates search and publication; form and content are regulated by Implementing Regulations (length/format).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority right and claiming priority (Articles 87–89)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority right — conditions and effect of claiming priority from an earlier application under the Paris Convention; how priority is claimed and effects on novelty and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules determine the priority date and thus what is prior art; procedural requirements for claiming priority (timing, documents) are critical to secure priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of filing and proceedings; translations; publication language (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Languages of the European Patent Office — official languages are English, French and German; applications must be filed in one of these languages or accompanied by a translation within time limits; translations of claims into the two other languages must be included for the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies filing-language options and mandatory translations; if required translation is not filed in time, document may be deemed not received; grants and publications rules depend on language of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on filing and formal examination (Part IV headings: Examination on filing; Examination of requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal examination on filing — Receiving Section examines formal requirements up to when request for examination is made; Examining Divisions examine substantive requirements upon request for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes formal vs substantive examination stages; applicants must request examination and meet formalities within prescribed time limits to proceed to substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: European search report (Article 92 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing up of the European search report — the Search Divisions are responsible for drawing up the search report covering the state of the art relevant to the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search report is a key procedural and substantive input; its content and timing affect prosecution strategy and decisions to request examination or amend claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination and time limits (Part IV headings and Art.95–98)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for examination — the applicant must, within specified periods, request substantive examination; rules provide for extensions and consequences of failure to request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing the request or failing to meet time limits can lead to deemed withdrawal or inability to obtain grant; Administrative Council may amend time limits per Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal or grant; publication of specification (Part IV headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal or grant — after examination the Examining Division shall decide to refuse or grant the European patent; on grant the specification is published in the language of proceedings with claim translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant triggers national effects in designated States; refusal can be appealed; publication formalities (translations) determine enforceability and rights in Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure and grounds for opposition (Part V: Articles 99–104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition — after grant, third parties may file oppositions within the time limit; grounds for opposition and the procedure for examination of opposition are defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition grounds (e.g., lack of novelty, inventive step, sufficiency) must be pleaded within prescribed time; Opposition Divisions decide on revocation or maintenance (possibly in amended form) and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of European patent and patent term (Part II, Chapter III: Articles 63–67)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of the European patent and rights conferred — the patent confers, in each designated Contracting State, the same effect and is subject to the same conditions as a national patent; term and rights are specified by the Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines territorial and substantive effects in each State, the term (duration) of protection, and translation obligations that affect enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of revocation and extent of protection (Articles 68–70 and Protocol on Article 69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of revocation — rules on consequences of revocation; extent of protection — Article 69 (and its Protocol) prescribes that the extent of protection is to be interpreted as a balance between literal claim wording and the description, providing fair protection and reasonable certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol cautions against extremes (strict literalism vs claims as mere guidelines) and mandates an intermediate interpretation combining fair protection for patentee with reasonable certainty for third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic text and translations of patent documents (Articles 68, 14, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic text of a European patent application or European patent — rules on which language/text is authentic and requirements for translations of the specification and claims into other official languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity and required translations affect enforceability and interpretation; entries in Register made in three languages, but language of proceedings is authentic in case of doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to apply and rights of inventor (Part II, Chapter II: Articles 58–62)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entitlement to file and right to a European patent — who may file and obtain a European patent, multiple applicants, applications by persons not having the right, and the inventor's right to be mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules determine legal ownership, multiple applicants' rights, and situations where the applicant may not be the entitled person; inventors have right to be mentioned subject to Convention provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the EPO; professional representatives (Part V, Chapter III: Articles 133–134)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation — general principles of representation and rules on professional representatives before the European Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when representation is required and qualifications/registration of professional representatives; affects who can act in proceedings on behalf of applicants/parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boards of Appeal: composition, independence and exclusion (Articles 21–24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards of Appeal — rules on composition of Boards for different appeals, appointment and independence of members, and exclusion/objection procedures for partiality or conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures impartial appellate review: members appointed for fixed terms and removable only for serious reasons; procedures exist to exclude or object to members with personal interest or prior involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations by third parties and oral proceedings (Articles 115–116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations by third parties — third parties may make observations concerning patentability; oral proceedings — parties may request oral proceedings in designated situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party observations can influence examination/opposition though they may not be party to proceedings; oral proceedings are procedural rights at certain stages and must be requested and scheduled per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking of evidence and procedural time limits (Articles 117–122)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking of evidence — rules for evidence gathering and evaluation in proceedings; Time limits — form and consequences of time limits, further processing and restitutio in integrum (restoration) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural evidentiary rules and strict time limits govern admissibility and ability to correct procedural defaults; provisions for further processing and restoration exist under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical opinions for national courts (Article 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical opinion — at the request of a competent national court, the European Patent Office shall, for a fee, give a technical opinion concerning a European patent which is the subject of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining Divisions issue such opinions; they are advisory and may assist national courts in infringement or revocation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council competences (Articles 33–36 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Council powers — competence to amend time limits, Implementing Regulations, Financial Regulations, Rules relating to Fees, service regulations and to adopt or amend various organizational provisions (including weighting of votes and voting rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Council decisions affect procedural and fee structures; some decisions require special majorities and can alter practical prosecution rules (e.g., time limits, composition of examining divisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion into national patent application and national effects (Part VII, Chapter I & Part VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion — provisions and formal requirements for requesting application of national procedure; impact of EPC proceedings on national law and conversion into national patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides route and formalities for converting a European application to a national procedure and addresses interaction between European and national patent systems.
